output.summary: A large deciduous tree native to much of Europe, especially humid climates. Young trees and clipped hedges often retain their dead leaves until spring. Its nuts are eaten, although large quantities are slightly toxic; historically they were pressed for cooking oil or soaked before being ground into flour.
output.edibilityNote: Nuts are eaten but are slightly toxic in large quantities; they were used for cooking oil or soaked to remove tannins before making flour.
